title: Natural cardinalities for a single possibly disconnected smooth proper curve
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, C a scheme with a structure morphism f:C→Spec k smooth of relative dimension one and proper, and n a natural number nonzero in k. Write c=Nat.card(ConnectedComponents C) and g=arithmeticGenus_k C=dim_k H^1(C,O_C). Then Nat.card H^0(C,Z/n)=n^c, Nat.card H^1(C,Z/n)=n^(2g), Nat.card H^2(C,Z/n)=n^c, and Nat.card H^r(C,Z/n)=1 for r>2, with the source Ext model of etale cohomology. C may be empty or disconnected; n need not be prime. This theorem is only the pointwise numerical part of lem-fin-projective-curve-betti-cardinalities and makes no assertion about a family or constructibility.

proof.text: Properness makes C Noetherian over the field. Index its finitely many clopen connected components by I=ConnectedComponents C, and realize each as the open subscheme U_i. The corresponding opens are disjoint and cover C. Their inclusions are also closed immersions. Restrict f to d_i:U_i→Spec k. Smooth relative dimension one survives restriction, and properness follows by composition with the closed immersion. Nonemptiness and the smooth dimension formula show that each d_i is a connected curve of dimension one, without point summands.

The structure sheaf has finite-dimensional coherent cohomology on the proper C. Apply the existing source finite-clopen dimension formula to its H^1. Pullback takes the structure module to the structure module. Serre duality on each smooth proper component identifies its arithmetic genus with d_i.genus. Consequently arithmeticGenus(C)=sum_i d_i.genus. This also proves the empty-sum case.

Apply the connected proper curve calculation to d_i and n. It gives additive equivalences to Z/n, (Fin(2*d_i.genus)→Z/n), and Z/n in degrees zero, one, and two, and subsingleton cohomology above degree two. This source theorem includes the primitive-root Kummer trivialization; no new root or global family of roots is chosen.

The open component inclusions have the coproduct universal property. finiteCoproductCohomologyAssembly identifies H^r(C,Z/n) with the product of the cohomologies of the restricted constant sheaves. upperStarConstantSheafIso identifies these coefficients with each U_i.constantZMod n. Nat.card_pi and the component equivalences give products of n, n^(2*d_i.genus), n, and one. Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum and the genus sum evaluate them as n^c, n^(2g), n^c, one. All cohomology groups are nonempty, including in vanishing degrees, so their subsingleton cardinality is one. Empty products are one.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_proper_curve_natural_cardinalities {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsProper f] (n : ℕ) (hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) : letI : C.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨f⟩ let c := Nat.card (_root_.ConnectedComponents C) let g := Scheme.arithmeticGenus k C Nat.card (Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod n) 0) = n ^ c ∧ Nat.card (Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod n) 1) = n ^ (2 * g) ∧ Nat.card (Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod n) 2) = n ^ c ∧ ∀ r, 2 < r → Nat.card (Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod n) r) = 1
